title: One fifth of pre-2014 Locarno count pairs cannot be pure size reweightings on an identical spot set
abstract: We test whether paired Locarno weighted and unweighted counts can isolate size weighting in the reported drift of sunspot number against emission indices. In archive version 2026A, unweighted counts exceed weighted counts in 18,233 of 89,115 valid group records dated 1957-2013 (20.46%), but in only 129 of 13,784 records dated 2014-2025 (0.94%). Pure size weighting on an identical spot set requires the opposite inequality. Complete drawing totals also fail this test on 20.00% of retained pre-2014 dates. Excluding those dates raises the older ratio of summed weighted to unweighted Wolf counts from 1.072 to 1.141. These results do not prove archive errors. The archive includes recounts of old drawings, which can change spot identification. A secondary emission-matched Cycle 24-25 decomposition has total-count intervals that include one and depends on observer and window. The paired fields alone do not identify a physical weighting change or the cause of index drift. We provide audit code, aggregate results, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions.

display.caption: A pure reweighting of an identical spot set needs W >= U. Older count pairs often fail this necessary test; a recount can explain the failure without a data error.
Exploratory Cycle 24-25 decomposition on common observation days and overlapping emission ranges. Conditional intervals omit count-method uncertainty.
